cards.text: VEL-COLETTE-LOOKRICH-01 · TALKING-HEAD CREATOR, PICK ONE

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Greenscreen talking-head candidates for the Colette look-rich ad. Nano Banana Pro i2i, anchored on DANA, the established Colette creator from the 8/16 linear-story run, so no new casting for this product. Wardrobe and prop mirrored from the reference reel: white ribbed tank, thin gold chain, small hoops, low loose bun, and a small black handheld content mic with a grey furry windscreen held at the chin. The mic is the format signature, it is what makes the ad read as a creator recording a voiceover rather than a commercial. FOUR generated, ONE pick. This is SOP step 2 of 4; animation needs the approved still plus the finished VO, so nothing renders until Brooks picks.
ANCHOR

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Dana, the established Colette creator
The identity reference from the 8/16 linear-story run. Supplied face, bone structure, skin tone and hair colour ONLY. Wardrobe, mic, lighting and the green all came from the prompt.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Continuity. Same woman across Colette content, per the one-creator lock.

No new casting for a product that already has a creator.
v1-white-a

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: PICK
Chest-up with headroom, eyes straight to lens, mouth open mid-sentence, mic at the chin in the right hand. White ribbed tank, thin gold chain, gold hoops, low loose bun with strands at the temples.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Warm, mid-thought, unperformed. Reads as someone talking, not presenting.

Best framing for a quarter-frame cutout and the cleanest identity match. Skin reads real: pores, fine lines, a little forehead shine. Green mean RGB 38/158/84, stdev 23.5.
v4-oatmeal

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: ALTERNATE, the despill-safe one
Same framing, oatmeal ribbed tank instead of white. Mic sits lower, at the chest rather than the chin.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Same register, slightly warmer and more autumnal.

FLATTEST GREEN of the four, stdev 10.0, and a warm garment is the safer despill. Loses a little of the reference grammar because the mic drops off the chin. Use this if the white tank keys pink.
v2-white-b

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: HOLD
Much tighter crop. Face fills the frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Fine performance, wrong scale.

Not enough body left for a small cutout, and the eyes drift camera-right instead of holding the lens.
v3-white-c

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: REJECT
Eyes off-lens, a second hand enters bottom-centre with broken anatomy, and the green carries a visible gradient in the upper left.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Reads as distracted, looking past camera.

Structural defect, not a note. Anatomy plus a non-flat plate.

cards.title: CANDIDATES · pick one  ·  Nano Banana Pro i2i · 1536x2752 · 2026-08-29

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: KEY WITH A TOLERANCE
cards.text: All four are keyable but none is a perfectly flat plate. Green stdev runs 10 to 27 across the set. Use a tolerance rather than a single-colour hard key, and pull the matte before judging the edge.

cards.title: DESPILL STAYS LOW
cards.text: At 0.5 a neutral garment against green renders PINK, and the pick is a white tank. Check the tank in pixels, not on the read. v4-oatmeal is the fallback if white will not behave.

cards.title: WHY THE MIC
cards.text: The reference creator holds a small handheld content mic near her chin. It is the single strongest signal in the format: it says creator recording a voiceover, which is why the ad reads as a recommendation rather than a commercial. Keep it in every frame.

cards.title: GATED, NOTHING RENDERS YET
cards.text: This is SOP step 2 of 4. Step 3 animates the approved still on the finished VO in HeyGen, and the VO does not exist yet. Storyboard-first law: pick the still, then VO (voice NBIPq5xdnIg9kaBH5Ape Woman Over 40, respell Vell-Ahn-Trah, STT gate, tighten, normalize to -14 LUFS), then HeyGen, then key, then comp.
